title: Telemetry-first tool alias resolution and stream handoff
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: OpenAI-style tool descriptors (name/description/schema) and legacy function signatures diverge. Existing name-matching heuristics are brittle during streaming when the model emits a tool call mid-response and the runtime must perform a zero-latency handoff to a legacy callback. This ticket designs and implements a telemetry-first alias resolver and a deterministic streaming handoff envelope that preserves provenance, minimizes false-positive matches, and enables rollback metrics for A/B-style compatibility shims.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a canonical alias resolver service that returns an ordered list of candidate mappings with scores and provenance tags within 15ms p95 for typical catalog size (<= 4k tool names)

Streaming handoff envelope defined and implemented: tool invocation metadata (canonical_id, alias_source, resolution_score, token_offset, model_version) is propagated to downstream callback executor and persisted in request trace
On ambiguous matches (score between 0.45 and 0.75) the runtime follows a configurable fallback policy: canary-to-legacy OR probabilistic-staging flag controlled by rollout config
End-to-end e2e tests exercising: exact match, prefix match, fuzzy match, name collision, simultaneous competing tool calls in a single stream
Dashboard widgets show alias_resolution_rate, handoff_latency_ms, ambiguity_rate, rollback_rate per release and per customer tier
No regression in streaming throughput: <= 5% p95 increase in streaming latency for baseline workloads when resolver enabled
implementation_notes: Alias resolver: lightweight trie + bloom filter precheck, followed by fuzzy edit-distance scoring (weighted by token-level similarity and description embedding cosine). Keep runtime-only cache with eviction by LRU and TTL=10m
Scoring: combine name exactness (0-1), schema compatibility (0-1), description embedding similarity (0-1) with weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 by default; expose weights via config

Streaming envelope: JSONL meta-chunks prefixed with special token <!HANDOFF> that includes canonical_id, alias_source (model-suggested | registry-alias | user-override), resolution_score, token_stream_offset, request_id, model_version
Backpressure: if resolver lookup or callback exec exceeds budget, the runtime emits an in-band fallback event to model (e.g., CALL_DECLINED_RETRY_LATER) and records telemetry
Compatibility shim behavior: runtime supports mapping tables that can be injected per-customer; these override resolver decisions and are auditable via audit log entries
Telemetry-first design: every resolution decision emits a minimal resolved_event to telemetry ingest with resolution_id to link traces, stored for 30 days by default
Persistence: resolved_event stored as part of request trace in tracing service; used by rollback jobs to replay ambiguous cases with alternate mapping
Security: no function arguments are exposed in alias lookup; only names, schemas hashes, and non-sensitive metadata are used for scoring
telemetry_metrics: alias_ambiguity_rate (fraction of resolutions where top_score - second_score < 0.15)
handoff_latency_ms (time from model emission to callback executor start)
rollback_rate (percentage of requests where mapping was changed post-handoff)
per-canonical-id invocation counts and failure rates
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable resolver for 1% traffic with deterministic fallback-to-legacy disabled; collect metrics for 72h
Phase 2 (probing): enable probabilistic legacy fallback for ambiguous buckets (score 0.45-0.75) at 10% within canary traffic; validate rollback_rate and customer errors
Phase 3 (gradual): increase to 10% global traffic if alias_ambiguity_rate < 2% and handoff_latency within SLO
Phase 4 (on by default): 100% rollout with customer-specific mapping injection enabled; provide opt-out via customer flags
Rollback criteria: ambiguity_rate > 5% for 24h OR increase in callback execution failures by > 1.5x
test_plan: Unit: alias resolver scoring combinations, trie edge cases, bloom filter false positives simulations
Integration: end-to-end streaming test harness that drives model-output fragments with embedded <!HANDOFF> markers and validates callback invocation trace
Load: resolver QPS at catalog sizes 1k, 4k, 10k to verify p95 latency targets
Chaos: simulate slow callback executor and assert in-band fallback signal and telemetry emitted
Regression: compare baseline streaming p95 with resolver disabled vs enabled using existing streaming-bench suite
